summary: Artemis Base Camp: Junior Astronaut Trainer is an interactive, browser-based educational simulator designed to teach students and aspiring explorers the core principles of lunar outpost management. Addressing the challenge of making complex space mission logistics accessible to young learners, the application puts players in command of a lunar habitat where they must balance power generation, oxygen production, and water reclamation across multiple mission sols (days). Using real parameters inspired by NASA’s Artemis program and lunar surface environment data, users experience firsthand how critical life-support trade-offs affect crew survival. Built as a lightweight, zero-installation web application, it empowers classrooms and independent learners worldwide to explore space engineering fundamentals.
details: The game is one HTML file built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no outside libraries or images. Players start with Power, Oxygen and Water at 70%. Each Sol they pick one of four actions: align solar arrays, run the oxygen reactor, mine crater ice, or conduct a science EVA. The first three give +25% to one resource and cost the others; the EVA costs all three but earns a science packet. Surviving 7 Sols earns a Junior Astronaut certification. The benefit is hands-on learning of life-support trade-offs. It is creative because it uses a short, replayable survival loop. We considered mobile use, simplicity and accessibility. Next steps are random events, longer missions and difficulty levels.
